 
Nepal Red Cross Society, Emergency Operation Center (EOC), Email: eoc@nrcs.org 
 
 
 
 
Situation Overview:  
 
 The situation after the recent flash flood in Rasuwa 
remains critical with significant loss of lives, many 
people are still missing along with the extensive 
damage to roads, bridges, electricity and 
communication infrastructure, and severe disruption 
to basic services across affected areas. Search and 
rescue operations are ongoing, while urgent 
humanitarian needs for food, safe drinking water, 
emergency shelter, healthcare, and other essential 
assistance continues to grow. Due to potential risk of 
rising flood, alert messages were disseminated to the 
community to remain safe. 
 
 Government Health Emergency Operation Centre 
(HEOC) has been activated. Bir Hospital, Teaching 
Hospital, Civil Hospital, Patan Hospital and Police Hospital are kept 
standby. 100/100 bed in Bir hospital and Trauma centre , 60 bed in 
Patan hospital has been allocated for providing free services to the 
affected and injured people .  Similarly, relief materials are being 
collected at the National Emergency Warehouse located at Tribhuvan 
International Airport, the Nepal Army’s Maithili Barracks in Battar, 
Nuwakot, and the Baireni Barracks in Dhading, and  arrangements 
have been dispatched to the affected areas based on needs and 
priorities. Government have announced to provide financial 
assistance for the families of deceased in accordance of prevailing 
laws along with free communication package targeting the affected 
people for providing easy access to get connected with their 
family. In addition, the Government of Nepal has appealed for 
financial contributions to the Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund in response to the recent flash flood. 
Contributions made to the Prime Minister’s Disaster Relief Fund are also eligible for deduction from 
taxable income under Section 12B (दफा १२ख) of the Income Tax Act, 2058. 
 
As of the latest updates  from NDRRMA situation report published on 28 August 2026,  579 dead 
bodies have been found and 1,924 are still missing whereas 4,451 people have been rescued. Rescue 
operations are ongoing, and the government has activated a multi -agency response to assess the 
damage and provide relief. In the flood -affected areas, 6,755 personnel from the Nepal Army, 4,473 
from the Nepal P olice, and 4,203 from the Armed Police Force Nepal have been deployed. The 
collection of details regarding human and physical losses is ongoing.  
 
 
 
Rasuwa Flood Situation Update 3  (28 August 2026)

Relief Item Dispatched from NRCS as of 28 
August 2026 
NRCS Response 
• Initial Rapid Assessment (IRA)  
-    15 volunteers in Nuwakot oriented on IRA and have been 
mobilized for data collection in the affected areas. 
-  IRA report of Nuwakot is collected and compiled 
• Restoring Family Link (RFL) Services:  
- Help desk established at Nuwakot supporting them 
to connect with their relatives through phone call 
- NRCS Chitwan district chapter mobilized volunteer 
for collection of antemortem data  
• Ready to eat food (RTEFs) distributed to around 750 
people in Nuwakot. 
(RTEFs include Noodles 1 packet, Biscuits 1 packet 
beaten rice 200 gram, Drinking water 1 bottle Per Person)  
• Relief items distribution: NRCS Nuwakot District 
Chapter has distributed the following relief items: 
o Blanket: 15 pcs, Mattress: 25 pcs 
o 21 Hygiene kits  
• 12 cartoons drinking water distributed 
*NRCS EOC is looking forward to detailed information and updated situations. NRCS along with 
IFRC and its network is also planning for emergency response and DREF application.
